name: Create Agent
description:
Creates a new agent at g/<agentId> in the caller's namespace. The name must be unused; an existing agent is an error. To replace an agent, explicitly call agent:delete with remove=true and then create the new agent. Use agent:update for history-preserving config or state changes.

Omit config for the recommended skilled default: read/list tools plus skills loaded on demand, using the venue's default transition and LLM provider. Pass config={} only when you intentionally want an explicit minimal configuration.

Custom example: agent_create(agentId='Helper', config={operation: 'v/ops/llmagent/chat', systemPrompt: 'You summarise documents.'}). The 'operation' field must be a resolvable lattice path (e.g. 'v/ops/llmagent/chat' for plain persona chat, 'v/ops/goaltree/chat' for goal-decomposing planners) — bare adapter shorthand like 'llmagent:chat' will not resolve. To use a different provider, set llmOperation in config (e.g. 'v/ops/langchain/anthropic' for Claude, 'v/ops/langchain/ollama' for local models); each provider op resolves its API key from the user's secret store via its own default secretKey, or you can override with apiKey='s/<SECRET_NAME>'. After creation, send work via agent_request and inspect via agent_info.

config.description: Agent configuration. Either an inline map or a string reference that resolves to one — workspace path (e.g. 'w/templates/reader'), asset ref (/a/<hash>), DID URL, or venue operation name. Key fields: operation (transition op as a full lattice path, e.g. 'v/ops/llmagent/chat'), systemPrompt (what the agent does), llmOperation (LLM provider op path, default 'v/ops/langchain/openai'; set to 'v/ops/langchain/anthropic' for Claude, etc.), model (LLM model id, default gpt-5.4-mini), apiKey (optional 's/<SECRET_NAME>' reference; otherwise the provider op's default secretKey is used), tools (array of operation lattice paths it can call, e.g. 'v/ops/covia/read' — not adapter shorthand like 'covia:read'), caps (capability restrictions). A resolved template may also include a 'state' field which is used as the agent's initial state.

operation.description: Transition operation for the agent — must be a resolvable lattice path (e.g. 'v/ops/llmagent/chat' for persona chat, 'v/ops/goaltree/chat' for goal-decomposing planners). Bare adapter shorthand like 'llmagent:chat' will NOT resolve. Determines how the agent processes tasks.

systemPrompt.description: System prompt defining the agent's role and behaviour

tools.description: Tool operations the agent can call, given as resolvable operation lattice paths (e.g. ['v/ops/covia/read', 'v/ops/covia/write']) — these reference operations, not adapters, so bare adapter shorthand like 'covia:read' will NOT resolve. (Harness tools such as 'subgoal' and 'context_load' are the exception: bare names, not operations.) This is the agent's exact allowlist — it is advertised only these tools unless defaultTools is true.

defaultTools.description: Opt into the built-in default tool pack — deliberately minimal, read-only workspace access (covia read/list) — on top of the declared tools. Defaults to false: the agent sees only its own 'tools' list. Capability tools (writes, agents, assets, grid, schema) arrive via skills (skill_load) or explicit 'tools' entries.

caps.description: Capability restrictions — array of {with, can} objects limiting what the agent can access

oneOf.description: Reference to a config map stored in workspace, assets, or elsewhere

definition.description: Asset ID of an agent definition using the legacy nested format (meta.agent.config). For the unified approach, pass the reference directly in 'config'.

status.description: Current status of the agent: SLEEPING, RUNNING, SUSPENDED, or TERMINATED

warnings.description: Optional non-fatal advisories; present and non-empty only when the config looks misconfigured but create still succeeded. Each entry is a human-readable message. Currently the only advisory: the agent declares tools on an Ollama model whose tool-calling support could not be confirmed (no 'tools' capability, or the model is not installed/reachable). Absent when there is nothing to flag.
